5.draft_content:
The proposed solution architecture for Acme Logistics will enable real-time integration between the new SAP S/4HANA Transportation Management (TM) environment and the existing Manhattan WMS, replacing the current nightly batch integration model used between the warehouse platform and SAP ECC for EDI 850 and 856 transaction processing. The target-state architecture is intended to support more timely transportation planning, execution visibility, and downstream coordination across order, warehouse, and carrier-related processes.

The solution will position SAP S/4HANA TM as the core transportation management platform within the target landscape. Manhattan WMS will remain in place as the warehouse execution system, with interface connectivity designed to support real-time data exchange between the two platforms. In addition, the target architecture will include a new interface to the Project44 carrier rate engine to support carrier-related integration requirements as part of the future-state transportation process.

The deployment model for the SAP S/4HANA TM solution is `<CONFIRM: deployment model for SAP S/4HANA TM, including hosting approach and environment landscape>`. The integration architecture, including middleware, API framework, message orchestration approach, error-handling design, monitoring framework, and retry mechanisms, is `<TECH TEAM: confirm integration platform and target-state interface design for S/4HANA TM, Manhattan WMS, and Project44>`.

The high-level architecture is expected to include the following components:
- SAP S/4HANA TM as the target transportation management application.
- Manhattan WMS as the retained warehouse management platform.
- Project44 as the carrier rate engine interface in the target state.
- Real-time interface connectivity between SAP S/4HANA TM and Manhattan WMS.
- A new interface between SAP S/4HANA TM and Project44.
- `<TECH TEAM: confirm whether any additional upstream or downstream systems are in scope for the target architecture>`.

Change governance for the solution architecture will be managed through the project governance and change control process defined elsewhere in this SOW. Any proposed change affecting the agreed architecture, deployment model, interface design, system boundaries, or non-functional requirements shall be reviewed for scope, timeline, resource, and commercial impact before implementation. Architecture decisions that remain open at the time of SOW finalization are listed in Section 21 (Key Observations) and, where applicable, shall be resolved prior to build execution.
